$comment: EXPLICITLY APPROVED BREAKING CONTRACT CHANGES. Read by build/scripts/openapi_diff.py.
A breaking change is a change that stops a client already built against the published contract
from working: an operation or response field removed, a request field made required, an enum
value a client may send taken away. CI fails on one. This file is how somebody says 'yes, and
here is why' — the decision is recorded where the next person can read it, rather than
suppressed by a flag, an environment variable or a commit-message keyword.
AN APPROVAL QUOTES THE FINDING VERBATIM, not a pattern. A pattern approves the change nobody
has looked at yet: the second removal under the same path, the one that was not in the pull
request the reviewer read. Run the comparator, copy the finding text from its output, paste it
here.
AND IT EXPIRES. An approval outliving the change it covered is a waiver sitting in the
repository waiting to cover an identical future change silently. Past expiresOn it stops
applying. Once the baseline is re-emitted and committed the approval matches nothing, the
comparator reports it as stale, and it should be deleted in that same change.
PREFER NOT NEEDING ONE. Versioning is in the URI segment (/v1/, /v2/), so the honest answer to
a breaking change is usually a new version rather than a mutation of the published one. Reach
for this file when a contract has no clients yet, or when every client is known and has already
migrated — and say which in the reason.
FIELDS, all required:
document        — the artifact path as the comparator prints it, forward slashes
(e.g. 'ragcore/customer.v1.openapi.json')
finding         — the finding text, verbatim, without the 'BREAKING ' prefix
approvedBy      — a person, not a team or a pipeline
approvedOn      — ISO date
expiresOn       — ISO date; after this the approval does not apply
reason          — why the change is acceptable rather than what it is
clientMigration — what somebody already calling the old contract has to do. 'none' only when
the contract genuinely has no clients, and say so.
